problem_type: credential persistence and catalog publication invariant regression
symptom: A newly saved onboarding API credential could fall back to plaintext when Electron safeStorage was unavailable; legacy plaintext could still be resolved by runtime execution and health probes; staged, failed, or wrong-mode adapter models could appear in production lists; malformed explicit capability contracts could publish and execute; old nodes could stay pinned to a disabled source model while a sibling kept that vendor alive; and equal connection settings could reuse a promoted candidate identity, overwrite its credential, or leave terminal candidate secrets and mappings orphaned.
direct_cause: The shared API-key writer returned enc=plain instead of failing and the shared execution decryptor returned legacy plaintext; Electron maintained a weaker capability-contract validator than the renderer parser; publication consumers used divergent enabled/adapter checks without exact task modes; the node resolver treated vendor availability as proof that its exact model remained executable; candidate identity was only a stable connection hash without a run revision or explicit root/parent lineage; terminal and delete paths did not cascade candidate state; and multi-model manual onboarding repeated independent credential/catalog transactions.
class_root: Credential readiness, formal capability validity, active model contracts, executable task modes, and candidate revision lineage were represented by permissive mutable fields at multiple consumers instead of being derived and committed at shared secure-storage, parser, resolver, publication-DTO, lifecycle, promotion, and catalog-transaction boundaries.
affected_population: Users creating or editing an authenticated model connection on a host where Electron safeStorage is unavailable or encryption fails
Users with legacy enc=plain or pre-encoding API-key records entering a new adapter authentication run
Users viewing MCP or normal model pickers while an onboarding model is staged, unverified, partially verified, or failed
Projects whose saved node still names a source vendor/model after verified promotion moved that model to a candidate revision
Users retrying, cancelling, superseding, or deleting provider-adapter candidate revisions
entry_points: CatalogMutation.upsertApiKey used by manual onboarding and provider-adapter register/stage writes
deriveModelListing for nomi_list_models and modelCatalogCache for normal renderer pickers
resolveExecutableNodeFromCatalog for persisted node vendor/model migration
Provider Adapter fail, cancel, stale, supersede, promote, and catalog vendor deletion lifecycle
internal_only_reason: This change enforces Nomi's approved internal persistence and promotion invariants. External provider or protocol behavior cannot decide whether local plaintext storage is acceptable or whether Nomi publishes an unverified catalog row.
invariants: Every new or edited authenticated credential is encrypted through safeStorage or the transaction throws before catalog persistence; thrown errors never contain the submitted secret.
Legacy plaintext remains structurally recognizable as needs_resave but is not credential-ready for a new authentication run.
The shared execution credential resolver returns plaintext only for decryptable safeStorage records; legacy material never reaches an execution request, health probe, error, or log.
Only verified executable modes enable new mappings and models; vendor enabled state is derived from at least one verified or preserved active executable model.
Unverified registration or credential re-save cannot replace any field of an already-published model contract; a verified promotion is the contract switch boundary.

An unverified endpoint, auth, header, provider-kind, or credential replacement is stored under a stable isolated candidate vendor identity; failure leaves the active shared vendor byte-identical and promotion switches only verified target models while preserving siblings.
Renderer model DTOs carry published and exact publishedModes derived in Electron from active revisions, custom calls, enabled mappings, or the text-only legacy path.
A legacy generic custom-call script publishes only the billing kind's minimal default task mode, while mode-specific scripts publish only task kinds proven by their explicit capability contract.

The shared capability manifest treats any present explicit contract as authoritative: all structural, kind, task, default, and uniqueness checks must pass, otherwise publication and runtime dispatch expose zero modes without built-in or generic fallback.

Renderer archetype resolution, Electron publication, and runtime custom-call dispatch use the same environment-neutral formal V1 capability parser, including intent, labels, hints, prompt requirements, slots, parameters, defaults, and collision checks.
A usable source vendor does not short-circuit node migration when its exact saved model is absent or disabled; resolver lineage continues across the full enabled catalog.

Every save or verification run against published execution gets a distinct candidate revision identity independent of secret material; only the same explicit unpublished run id may reuse its candidate.
Candidate metadata records root/revision identity plus a model-to-predecessor vendor and published-mode map; multi-model saves never infer one shared source vendor when active models span revisions.
Fail, cancel, timeout, stale, and cross-revision supersede remove the full unpublished candidate vendor/credential/model/mapping lineage before a terminal success can be persisted.
Promotion returns an explicit committed or no-lease result; only a committed non-empty verified-mode set may persist completed/partial run state or a revision.

Deleting a root vendor cascades all candidate descendants; deleting a promoted candidate removes its descendants and restores every model/mode snapshot actually disabled at promotion, including modes that failed on the candidate.
Catalog health counts a credential or authenticated executable model only when apiKeyDecryptStatus is ok, and reports locked versus needs_resave distinctly.
A multi-model manual onboarding save validates every candidate first, encrypts once per vendor, and commits every vendor/model/mapping change in one catalog mutation.
An enabled model with an existing custom-call, executable mapping, or active adapter revision remains published during credential re-save or a failed repair.

Unverified staged rows stay visible in settings metadata but are excluded from nomi_list_models and normal pickers, while legacy catalog rows and models with a preserved active revision remain available.
Production node and batch pickers pass the current executable task mode through the catalog cache, and batch model changes apply only to nodes in the same task-mode group.
migration: Existing enc=plain and encoding-absent records remain in place and are reported as needs_resave so the UI can request an explicit credential re-save. Their plaintext is not returned by the execution decryptor, sent to providers, silently re-encrypted, or admitted to a new certification run. Only legacy text models retain the historical adapter-less direct path; media models require an active revision, enabled executable mapping, or conservatively published custom call. An adapter model with an activeRevision remains published while a repair run is staged or fails. Replacing published execution creates an isolated root/parent/revision candidate vendor; successful verified promotion disables only the replaced source model and its exact mappings, old nodes resolve to the enabled revision, terminal unpublished candidates are removed atomically, and deleting a promoted revision restores its immediate source execution.
residual_risks: Legacy plaintext remains present on disk until the user explicitly re-saves or removes it; this task prevents new plaintext writes but does not destructively delete migration evidence.
Settings surfaces intentionally continue to show configured unverified rows so users can repair them; only production selection surfaces are verified-only.
Catalog rows predating adapter metadata retain compatibility only for text, whose historical direct AI SDK path is executable without a mapping.
